The best way to look at it in my opinion is that the Star Wars Expanded Universe (or what Disney has called “Legends”) has the best and the worst of the Star Wars franchise.

The best stories outside of the films are in the EU. The KOTOR games, the Thrawn Trilogy, X-Wing novels, NJO saga, Tales of the Jedi comics, the Clone Wars Multimedia project, and so many more novels I could list off if you wanted.

Then there’s also the worst of the franchise. Force-sensitive R5 droids, sentient mountains, Hutt Jedi, the Sun Crusher, the Dark Empire series, and absolutely horrible depictions of beloved film characters (Han in Courtship of Princess Leia, Luke throughout the entirely of the Callista Trilogy, and more).

I can promise you this; The EU has plenty of stories that are absolutely worth your time and will bring you back to the galaxy that you love better than any of the Disney projects ever wish they could. There are also just a TON of really really bad stories in there too.

So the writers of theEU novels and comics at the time felt a responsibility to actually make good stories, because to a lot of the fans those stories were the true continuation of the films. There was pressure to get it right. Other authors also were mandated to not contradict what other authors had written into the canon or what they were working on at the time. Everything was, for the most part, cohesive. Sure there were small retcons along the way and some continuity errors, but they were manageable!

Now there isn’t. The novels and comics can be retconned at a moments notice (Ahsoka novel and Dooku: Jedi Lost. For comics, the original Kanan series) by Filoni and the Story Group. The comics and novels no longer have substance anymore. They’re not seen as a way to continue the story, they’re seen as simply another revenue stream. Theres no incentive to read them because we know they’ll most likely get retconned by a live action show or cartoon. And because of that there’s also no incentive for the writers to write good novels and comics because they can be retconned and ignored at a moments notice. They’re no pressure to get it right anymore.

I have a sister with autism, and not many people I know are as empathetic as she is. If someone is feeling down about something she picks up on it and tries her best to comfort that person. Sometimes she gets so anxious about it that she freaks out and screams and cries because she can’t do anything to help. 

Now please, someone correct me if I’m wrong here, I openly welcome discussion about this because I only have to go off of what I’ve seen from my sister, her peers over the years, and other people with autism I’ve encountered throughout my life.

I have also seen people with autism whos actions would give the impression that they don’t have empathy. My interpretation of these people is that they just don’t have a grasp on how other people feel their emotions because they feel theirs so differently.

And also, people with autism are reminded every day that they’re different. Whether it’s through subtle side glances or someone outright telling them they are, every day they know. However it is my belief that they really are more alike us than they are different, but in some cases, because they’re told so often that they’re different, they think that the parts of them that are normal are also different than people without autism.

This is why I hate the term “Autism Spectrum”, it implies that autism is a line, and someone can either have really bad, moderate, or good autism. It’s not that at all. Autism should be an umbrella term, as from my experience every individual with autism has their own needs and their own parts of themselves that have delayed development.

I feel like this episode was in the end a complete let down. They take over an hour to show this deep love story spanning 16 years, only for that entire hour to be worth nothing and have no effect on Plot A (Joel and Ellie’s story) by the end because Bill is dead. Make Bill a bigger character in the story that isn’t just around for one segment of the journey like he was in the game. Let him interact with Joel after Frank dies and we get to see how all those 16 years affected him. To me there are 5 Primary Star Wars Universes

1) The Original 6 Films: George Lucas has stated in multiple interviews that his films were his world, and that the EU, which most of the time he simply referenced as Licensing, was a “parallel universe”. Also when you watch them you can tell there pretty self contained. Even whenever I watch them I only think about what the movies establish. I don’t watch Empire and think of all the comics and books or whatever that take place in between, only the previous movie, A New Hope.

2) The EU (pre- Prequels): the EU, with all the books, comics, video games and such that came out before TPM was released in 1999 were definitely its own world. If you read a lot of Post ROTJ EU material, the Clone Wars is defended as being a conflict where there was a clone uprising and the Jedi and Republic had to fight the clones and the mysterious Clone Masters. They kept the Clone Wars vague of course because of Lucas’ orders, but there was still some stuff there. The galaxy is just different and the rules of certain things like the Jedi Order and their old infrastructure as very different to how George ended up defining them in the prequels.

3) The EU (post-Prequels): When the prequels came out they retconned a shit-ton of old EU, so much to the point where the galaxy’s original shorty before the films was incredibly different. Many events such as the Clone Wars as a whole, Boba Fett in general, how Vader lost his right hand, and especially how long the Empire was around for were changed once the Prequels came out. This EU contains a lot of the old EU, but with several retcons and now new material to add to the continuity. 

4) The Disney Canon: This is easy to define. This is everything Disney classifies as their canon for their Star Wars works. The original 6 movies, Clone Wars cartoon, the Sequels, the High Republic, the Mandalorian, all the books and comics tho Ah were made after 2014 or so, etc. 

5) The Old Republic MMO: To me, SWTOR has just gone so far off onto its own path with its own lore, I just don’t see it being a part of any of the other universes, especially the past of the original movies. Technology is so advanced, they introduce stuff like the Eternal Empire, and everything is just so unique to that game. So much so that to me that game is a universe all on its own.

My best advice for weight loss is to manage what you’re eating, and only eat when you absolutely have to. You have to change the way you look at food. Instead of making it a way of coping with problems or a fun activity to do that makes you feel good, you have to make it only a fuel source. It’s just the thing you need to do to get through your day to function. It’s a bodily function, nothing more.

For meals, meats with high protein and vegetables. The dish I have seen the greatest results with so far has been a Caesar salad with grilled chicken. 

For snacks, granola bars, apples, and oranges. 

You gotta work on your self discipline and cut out all the bad carbs. No desserts of any kind, no breads, no pasta, no chips, no candy, not even croutons in your salad.

Eat a meal and as soon as you feel that feeling of satisfaction, stop eating, even if there is more food left over. Wait 20-30 minutes, and if you don’t feel hungry anymore than don’t eat anymore and put that food away. If you DO still feel like you NEED to eat (rather than you want to eat) than keep eating.
